hunts.label: Sunday, Nov 1
hunts.subtitle: An extra hour of sleep, a quiet swamp, and a deer that has not read the plan.

rules.title: Sunday is not Saturday (and the clocks changed)
items: **Clocks went back one hour at 2:00 am.** Every time on this page is the time on your clock Sunday morning. Sunrise is about 6:30 am and legal light is about 6:00 am on the new clock.
**Hunter orange is required** for firearm hunters (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Hat and vest on.
**Stop by 9:30 am.** Plan to be unloaded and out at 9:00.
**All migratory birds are closed on Sundays:** no ducks, doves, rails, woodcock, snipe or crow. Leave them alone today.
rules.note: Confirm Sunday rules in the NCWRC Regulations Digest. Check that your phone and watch both show the new time before you leave.

conditions.source: Source: hourly point forecast from a commercial weather service (the National Weather Service page was out of date for this day). Sun times from a published sun table.
items: **Walk-in, 4:50 am:** about 48°F. Nearly calm, a whisper from the north-northeast. Cloudy-ish.
**9 am:** about 58°F. Northeast wind near 5 mph. Warming fast after 8.
**Precipitation:** 6% or less all morning. Humidity 88 to 90% before sunrise, so damp leaves and maybe dew.
**Moon:** last quarter, about 50% lit. High in the sky near dawn.
conditions.meaning: **What it likely means (my assumption, not proven):** a mild, quiet morning with a moon overhead means deer may have fed late and could move later than usual, 6:30 to 8:30, with the warm-up near 8 pulling them toward bedding. Still air carries sound and scent in odd ways, so move slowly and trust the thread over the forecast.
conditions.hours_note: No gusts listed. Precipitation chance 6% at first, 1% by 9 am. Coldest point is about 6 am. Winds this light can swirl, so check the thread.

wind.label: from the NNE, nearly calm, about 1 to 2 mph, rising to 5 NE by 9 am

in_season: **Deer, either sex** (gun season, day 16). Pre-rut: bucks are cruising and checking does.
Quail and turkey are not open yet. Quail opens Nov 21.

in_season.tip: Bobcat is open and bear opens Nov 14. You are not hunting either. Slugs stay zipped, for defense only.

in_season: Closed today: ducks, doves, rails, woodcock, snipe and crow. Migratory birds are closed on Sundays.

plan.title: The plan: the Lodge Bend, sitting cross-wind to the swamp trail
plan.why: **Why here:** the swamp trail runs east and west along the water. Sit 40 yards SOUTH of it at the bend nearest the beaver lodge, on a slight rise if you can find one, back against a wide trunk, facing N, NW and NE. A deer walking the lane crosses in front of you, so a light north wind blows your scent south, away from the lane and the swamp corridor. It is also new ground, so you learn the land. **Caution:** at 1 to 2 mph the cold air may creep downhill toward the swamp. The thread will tell you. **Timing:** legal light is 6:00. Be seated about 45 minutes earlier, around 5:15. Leave the yard at 4:50. The extra hour of clock change does not change your body, so sleep when you can.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail, NE to the Junction. Red light low. Three steps, listen, three steps.
At the Junction turn east along the swamp. Find the bend where the water curls closest to the beaver lodge. Step 40 yards south of the water and pick a trunk wider than your shoulders.
Sit with your back to the trunk. Face N, NW and NE. Check what is behind every lane. No house, no field, nothing south, southwest or southeast.
Load at the sit, muzzle pointing N. Safety on. Tie a 12-inch thread to the barrel. If it points north steadily, your scent is going toward the lane. Slide 20 yards west or east and sit again.
Legal light. Scan the swamp edge and lane in sectors, left to right. Look for an ear, a leg, a flicking tail.
No deer? Stay another 30 minutes. The warm-up can send a late feeder past you toward bedding.
Swap 00 for #4. Walk the loop trail south, slow, for squirrel and rabbit. Shoot N, NW, NE, E or W only, never toward the house or field.
Walk the carry-out route you scouted Saturday, from the loop back toward the yard. Count the steps.
Unloaded and out at the yard edge, 30 minutes before the legal stop. Log what you saw with a "note:" message.

items: **In the gun:** 00 buckshot in the magazine. Modified choke. Safety on.
**Right pocket:** #4 and #7.5 birdshot. Swap in at about 8:30.
**Also carry:** knife, hatchet, gloves, 12-inch thread, 10 feet of cord, dry layer.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot.
Never shoot buckshot or slugs without the ground behind the target.
Keep buckshot and birdshot in different pockets. Check by feel.

animals.name: Deer
paragraphs: **Local:** common. They bed in the swamp thickets and travel the swamp edge toward the pasture side.
**Today:** pre-rut, mild, near calm, moon overhead. Best window (assumption): 6:30 to 8:30, with a late feeder possible near the warm-up.
**Shot:** broadside or quartering away only. 30 yards maximum with 00. Aim behind the front shoulder, middle of the body. Shoot only N, NW, NE, E or W. Never south.

details.title: Technique: scan by sectors, then move slowly
steps: Split the view into three sectors: left, center, right.
Look at the near ground first, then the middle, then the far edge of each sector.
Spend 10 seconds per sector. Move your eyes, not your head.
If you walk, take one slow step, then look for ten seconds. Deer see motion before shape.
details.note: Deer are the color of the woods. You will see a piece of a deer first, not the whole animal.

after: **Tip:** in still air, deer often hear you before they smell you. Keep your gear quiet and your coat from scraping bark.
**Tip:** if you take a deer, plan the drag route as in the Skill tab before you touch it.

animals.name: Squirrel
paragraphs: **Local:** gray squirrels are seen often. Fox squirrel is possible.
**Today:** a mild morning, so they feed early and stay active. (Assumption.)
**Shot:** head and neck. #4 to 30 yards. #7.5 to 25 yards. Only with a trunk or the ground behind it.

details.title: Technique: follow the debris to the feeder
steps: Look on the ground for fresh bits: green pine cone scales, nut husks, or holly berry skins.
Fresh debris means a feeder right above. Look straight up, along the sunlit side of the limbs.
Stand still and wait. A squirrel hides behind a limb but cannot resist a peek.
Shoot when the head shows. Mark where it falls by a nearby trunk.

after: **Tip:** a squirrel flat on a limb is usually watching you. Do not stare. Look slightly past it and wait.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: **Local:** likely at the feed bins and along thick edges of the loop.
**Shot:** #4 to 30 yards, N, NW, NE, E or W only.

details.title: Technique: circle the brush pile
steps: Find a brush pile or thick tangle near the loop.
Walk a slow half circle around it, about 10 yards out.
Stop every few steps and look low for an eye or an ear tip.
Check which way you will shoot before you step. If the rabbit bolts south, let it go.

after: **Safety:** wear gloves when you handle it. Check the liver for white spots.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Opportunity only. A raccoon or opossum heading to a den near the bins at dawn is possible.
**Look for:** the opossum track looks like a small hand with a thumb sticking out sideways. Same shot rules as above. Never toward the house or field.

skill.title: Skill of the week: plan the carry-out before you ever shoot
skill.principle: **Core principle:** a deer is heavy and the warm hours are short. Decide the drag route and what you carry before the shot. This is the same lesson as Saturday. Run it again from a different spot.

sections.title: Plan the route (do this today)
steps: 1. From your sit, walk the easiest path to the main trail. Count the steps.
2. Note any ditch, fallen log, or thick brush on that path. Pick a way around.
3. The land slopes up toward the yard. A drag toward the yard is uphill, so plan rests every 50 yards.
4. Cut about 10 feet of cord now and keep it in your pocket. Tie it around the front legs or the neck for a head-first drag.
5. Always drag head first. The hair lies flat and the body slides.

sections.title: After the shot (read this once)
steps: 1. Wait with the gun down for 30 minutes. Mark the spot where the deer stood.
2. Follow the blood trail slowly, using the blood trailing lesson.
3. Field dress it, then start cooling the meat within one hour.
4. Check the Digest for how and when to report the harvest.

details.title: Tap to open: why plan before the shot
paragraphs: Excited hunters forget details. If the route is already in your head, you can focus on the meat. Walking the route once, without a deer, costs nothing. Today you try it from a new sit, so you learn a second route.

skill.checkpoint: **Checkpoint:** on the walk out, count the steps from the Lodge Bend sit to the main trail. Send it in a "note:" message.

land.intro: Saturday you learned the Lower Pines stretch. Today you tie it to the swamp edge. Make notes on the walk out.
steps: Count your steps from the yard to the Junction, and from the Junction to the Lodge Bend sit.
Check the main trail where you looked Saturday. Look for new deer tracks across it, made overnight. Note which way they point.
Look near the lodge bend for tracks in mud and any trail worn through the leaves. Note where it leads.
Run the thread test at 5:20 and 8:00. Write down which way it points.
Send a "note:" message with what you found. Next week's plan will use it.

safety: **Shooting arc:** north, northwest and northeast. Never beyond east or west. NEVER south. The house is SW, the field is SE, the neighbor is south.
Buckshot and slugs need the ground behind them.
Hunter orange on, hat and vest. The 9:30 am stop is a hard limit. Be unloaded at 9:00.
Cool at dawn, about 48°F, and the clock change means it feels dark early. Bring a dry layer and gloves. Do not let numb hands handle the gun.
Walk in the dark with the red light. Watch for roots, holes and stumps near the swamp edge.
Bear and fox are in the area. Slugs are for defense only.
hunts.regs: Check the NCWRC Regulations Digest for Sunday hunting rules, deer reporting and bag limits.
hunts.gaps: No hunting entries in your Daily Notes this week. The National Weather Service page was out of date, so the hourly table came from another forecast service and its time zone was not stated; I assumed your clock after the change. I could not find moonrise or moonset times. Moon phase is from a calendar, not a local table.
